To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) HPV 6 and 11 were the predominant HPV genotypes in Chinese CA patients; 2) HPV 6 was more common than HPV 11; 3) HPV 16 was rarely detected in our CA patients; 4) HPV 18 was not detected in any of our patients; 5) there was a statistically significant correlation between HPV 6 and the clinical features; 6) there was no significant association between the clinical features and the HPV genotypes;
HPV types 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, and 33 are associated with CA.

1) HPV types are correlated with the location, age and sex of CA patients; 2) The most common types of HPV in CA are HPV6 and HPV11; 3) HPV6 and HPV16 were more prevalent in CA patients than in healthy controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical and histological features of condyloma acu- minimatum (CA).
the correlation of human papilloma virus with clinical features of condyloma acumi-natum.
the correlation of HPV types with the clinical features of patients diagnosed with condyloma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear evidence that the use of HPV vaccines is associated with an increased risk of genital warts.
HPV types are associated with clinical features, but the correlation is complex and not well understood.
there is no correlation between HPV types with the clinical features of condyloma acumenatum in China.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPV types were associated with the clinical features of condyloma acuminate in China.

we have demonstrated that HPV 6, 11, 40, 42, 43, 44, 54, 61, 62 and 66 were the main HPV types detected in patients with CA in China and that the clinical features of patients infected with HPV 6 and HPV 11 were similar.
HPV16 and HPV18 are the most common HPV types, and HPV6 and HPV11 are the most common non-HPV16/18 types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPV 6 and 11 are the most common types of HPV associated with condyloma, with a high correlation with clinical features such as age, sex, number and site of condyloma.
there is a significant difference in HPV type distribution between CA patients with and without concomitant high-risk HPV-related disease.
HPV 16 and 18 are more prevalent in CA patients than in the general population.
